archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area)
archetype.definition: With the deep game gone and his legs barely used this year, Jones is living on throws under 10 yards and a strong run game, which only works if the turnovers stay down, and they haven't.

report.headline: Last year's breakout has vanished; nothing past ten yards is working.
report.take:
Daniel Jones arrived in Indianapolis off a 2025 that looked like a career reset: 8.08 yards per attempt, +0.193 EPA per play, a 68% completion rate. Nine games into 2026 he is back near the floor of his Giants years. He sits at -0.188 EPA per dropback (40th of 49), 5.7 yards per attempt (41st), and a CPOE of -4.42. That CPOE is down 6.7 points from last season. The Colts are 2-7 and have lost five straight. The closest match in his career is the injury-shortened 2023 at -0.214. Read with that in mind, his career has two good seasons, 2022 and 2025, around a lot of below-average football. The 2025 year now looks more like the outlier than the new baseline.

The decline is almost entirely downfield. Under 10 air yards he is roughly average (-0.009 EPA, 71% completions, all six of his passing TDs). At 10+ air yards he is 36.3% with no touchdowns and seven interceptions. Deep balls have been close to unplayable: 12.1% completions, a CPOE of -25.1, -17.8 EPA on 33 throws. Alec Pierce, the vertical receiver, played only two games before landing on IR. That's the clearest football explanation. Jones's aggressiveness is also down 4.4 points, and his bad-throw rate is up 2.5 on last year, so it isn't only personnel. He is throwing into fewer tight windows and missing more of the open ones.

The second problem is ball security. He ranks 47th of 49 in interceptions and 45th in fumbles lost, on pace for 19 picks. The line hasn't helped: the offense is 28th in the rate its QB gets hit, and he's hit or sacked on 18.5% of dropbacks. His 31.4% pressure-to-sack rate is close to his career norm, though, so that part is who he is, not a new flaw. Tyler Warren, the third-most targeted player, has produced -0.22 EPA per target, and middle-of-the-field throws carry a -10.1 CPOE. The usable passing game has narrowed to Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

The last three games were the worst stretch: -0.355 EPA per dropback, a 9.7% sack rate, a 4.8% interception rate. Two of those came against the No. 1 and No. 3 defenses, so some of it is schedule. But the Dallas game, against the 31st-ranked defense, was still -8.6 EPA with a -9.5 CPOE. That keeps this from being explained away as a tough slate.

strengths.title: Short game still holds up
strengths.body: Throws of 0-9 air yards produce +0.079 EPA with a 50.6% success rate, and every one of his passing TDs has come from that range. It's the part of his game that matches his career: quick, on-schedule throws behind a good run game. It should hold, but it can't carry an offense when everything longer is negative.

strengths.title: Downs and Allen are reliable
strengths.body: Josh Downs (+0.266 EPA per target) and Keenan Allen (+0.168) are the only high-volume targets returning positive value. Both win underneath, which fits what Jones can currently execute. Any recovery runs through them, not through Warren or targets to the back.

strengths.title: Short-yardage legs and run support
strengths.body: His 13 designed runs have an 84.6% success rate and +0.669 EPA. Those are sneaks and short-yardage keepers, not big gains (1.92 yards a carry). The Colts' run game ranks 6th in EPA, which keeps the offense from fully collapsing. Scrambling, a former strength, has mostly disappeared (-0.155 EPA per scramble).

concerns.title: No passing game beyond ten yards
concerns.body: At 10+ air yards he has seven interceptions, no TDs and a -12 CPOE. Deep throws complete at 12.1%. Pierce's absence explains part of it, since he was the field-stretcher. Lower aggressiveness and more bad throws say Jones himself is also off, so his return isn't an automatic fix.

concerns.title: Turnovers on both fronts
concerns.body: He ranks near the bottom of the league in interceptions and in fumbles lost. The interceptions are a long-running career trait, and the 10+ air-yard throws are where most of them come from. Fumble luck may ease, but the interception rate is structural until the intermediate game is fixed.

concerns.title: Protection about to thin
concerns.body: The offense already ranks 28th in QB hit rate. Right tackle Jalen Travis, a 93%-snap starter, is expected to miss two to four weeks with a knee injury. Jones's sack rate has jumped to 9.7% over the last three games. With his history of taking sacks under pressure, a weaker edge compounds the problem.

trend.note: His only positive-EPA game came in Week 2. The five-game losing streak has produced his worst efficiency, peaking at -0.355 EPA per dropback over Weeks 7-9, and that included a poor game against a bottom-two defense.

nextGame.headline: Worst defense in football arrives at the right time
nextGame.body:
Miami ranks 32nd in defensive EPA, 31st against the pass and 32nd in success rate allowed. It is 30th on deep throws, giving up +1.136 EPA per attempt. Its pass rush is weak too, 28th in sack rate, which partly offsets the protection hit. If his deep ball shows up anywhere, it should be here. The Dolphins also leak to tight ends (32nd in TE1 EPA per target) and see an above-average share of targets go to TEs and backs. That gives Warren a soft matchup to finally pay off his volume. Outside receivers have been held under their fantasy averages, but they've still been efficient against Miami, so treat that split as noise from a small sample.

On the Colts' side, Travis's absence at tackle matters most, though Miami's weak rush lowers the stakes this week. Pierce remains on IR with no timetable, so the vertical threat is still missing. Mo Alie-Cox (groin) is a part-time tight end. Miami QB Malik Willis is questionable, and its offense is 26th in EPA and among the most run-heavy in the league. Combined with a 40.5 total, that points to a slower game where Indianapolis can lean on its run game. That lowers Jones's volume ceiling even in a good efficiency spot.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a broken secondary
keyMatchups.body: Jones is completing 12.1% of throws of 20+ yards. Miami allows +1.136 EPA on deep attempts. Something has to give. One or two completions would change his day, but his own deep accuracy is the bigger question than the coverage.

keyMatchups.title: Warren against a soft TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Warren has been a drag on efficiency at -0.22 EPA per target. Miami is the worst defense in the league against TE1s by EPA and sees a higher TE target share than the league norm. This is the week the middle of the field should open up.

keyMatchups.title: Weak rush versus thinner line
keyMatchups.body: Miami ranks 28th in sack rate, which gives a line missing Travis some margin. If Jones still takes three-plus sacks here, that points to him rather than the blocking.

nextGame.watch: Whether he completes anything 20+ yards downfield against a defense that gives up more on deep throws than almost anyone.

restOfSeason.body:
The short passing game, the run support and his sack tendencies are stable, and they define a below-average but functional quarterback. What's unsustainable is how bad the 10+ air-yard results are. A 12.1% deep completion rate is extreme even for a struggling passer, and some recovery is likely, especially if Pierce returns. Expect efficiency to drift up from the last-three-game low toward his career middle. A return to his 2025 level is unlikely: aggressiveness and accuracy both fell, not just the supporting cast. Interceptions stay a problem, so expect roughly 175-225 passing yards, under one TD and about one interception a game, with rushing mostly limited to sneaks.

The Travis injury sets a two-to-four-week window where protection is shakier. A 2-7 record also adds outside risk to his job security, though the dossier lists him as QB1 with no change.
swingFactors: Alec Pierce's return and the deep game with it
Whether a soft stretch of defenses steadies the turnovers

confidence.note: Nine starts with a clear direction, but Pierce's return and opponent quality could swing it.
